issue.standard_remedy: Consolidate tail suppliers into preferred suppliers
issue.summary: 127 of 160 suppliers share the last 20% of category spend

plan.diagnosis: Aluminium extrusions category exhibits extreme supplier fragmentation with 127 of 160 suppliers (79%) accounting for only 20% of spend (USD 3,770,677), while the HHI of 732 indicates low concentration. The tail comprises high-touch, low-value relationships that generate administrative overhead without leveraging volume for better pricing or terms.

remedy_steps.step: Conduct RFQ to consolidate tail spend (USD 3,770,677 from 127 suppliers) into 3-5 preferred tier-2 suppliers alongside top supplier Bauer Adv. Metals K.K. (20.7% share); target 8-12% price reduction on consolidated volume

Negotiate frame agreements with selected consolidation partners, incorporating volume commitments, tiered pricing, and standardized payment terms (Net 60); establish Bauer Adv. Metals K.K. as primary (50% allocation target) and 2-3 tier-2 suppliers
Implement systematic phase-out of 120+ tail suppliers through purchase order redirection and supplier exit communications; migrate active SKUs to consolidated supplier base
Update ERP master data across all systems to reflect new supplier hierarchy, block inactive tail suppliers, and enforce sourcing rules through approved vendor lists and catalog restrictions

Establish quarterly business reviews with tier-1 and tier-2 suppliers to monitor performance, volume compliance, and continuous improvement opportunities; track HHI improvement toward 1,500-2,000 target range

plan.expected_impact: Consolidation of USD 3,770,677 tail spend into preferred suppliers will yield USD 301,654 to USD 452,481 in annual savings (8-12% reduction) plus administrative cost avoidance from eliminating 120+ low-value supplier relationships.
kpis: Supplier count reduction from 160 to 35-40 within 6 months
Tail spend reduction from 20% to under 5% of category spend
Cost savings of USD 301,654-452,481 (8-12% on tail spend)
PO line item reduction of 60%+ in aluminium extrusions category
Supplier onboarding/maintenance cost reduction of USD 150,000+ annually
risks: Supply continuity disruption during transition if incumbents are exited before alternates are qualified
Quality variation from new tier-2 suppliers if technical specifications and metallurgical requirements are not rigorously validated
Resistance from business units with entrenched relationships to niche tail suppliers
Increased concentration risk if top supplier (Bauer Adv. Metals K.K.) allocation exceeds 50% without adequate backup sources
ERP data synchronization failures across 5 systems (SAP, Oracle EBS, Dynamics 365, NetSuite, Coupa) causing maverick buying
erp_actions: SAP: Apply posting block in LFA1 and purchasing block in LFB1 for 120+ tail suppliers being phased out; update source lists (EINA/EINE) to designate Bauer Adv. Metals K.K. and 2-3 tier-2 suppliers as preferred sources with validity dates

Oracle EBS: Inactivate 120+ tail supplier sites in PO module; create Approved Supplier List (ASL) entries for consolidated suppliers with rank 1 (Bauer) and rank 2 (tier-2 suppliers); update payment terms to Net 60 in supplier master

Dynamics 365: Set vendor status to 'Inactive' for tail suppliers; configure trade agreements for consolidated suppliers with tiered pricing based on volume thresholds; enable purchase agreement enforcement in procurement parameters

NetSuite: Mark 120+ tail vendors as inactive; create vendor bill approval workflows requiring Category Manager sign-off for any purchases outside approved aluminium extrusions vendor list; update preferred vendor fields on item records

Coupa: Remove tail suppliers from supplier catalog; configure guided buying rules to route all aluminium extrusions requisitions to approved supplier forms with Bauer and tier-2 suppliers only; set up spend alerts for non-catalog purchases over USD 500
